messages:

Cc: procurement@helixmed.com, dpo@helixmed.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Custody model + operator access for private deployment

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and privacy have a few outstanding asks before we can sign Dedicated/Private: specific language or artifacts that spell out who has custody of keys, when Redwood will have operator access, and what breakglass processes look like for VPC and on-prem patterns.

Specifically we need:
- A concise runbook or matrix showing responsibilities for keystore ownership (customer KMS vs Redwood-managed) across VPC and on-prem deployments.
- Confirmation on whether Redwood personnel can ever access customer plaintext or unencrypted token stores; if yes, under what circumstances and with what approval/recording.
- A list of subprocessors/subcontractors that would touch logs or telemetry in Private deployments and any planned subprocessor notifications.
- Preferred contractual language for an addendum to the DPA (we can sign via DocuSign).

Can you share these artifacts and indicate timelines? Our legal team would like to review before the end of this month.

Best,
Maya Devlin
Head of Procurement, HelixMed

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Devlin <m.devlin@helixmed.com>
Cc: procurement@helixmed.com, dpo@helixmed.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custody model + operator access for private deployment

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Looping you in with our internal privacy and product ops folks for the technical addendum; below is a short summary and I've attached a one-page matrix and a suggested DPA addendum draft for review.

Executive summary (short):
- Keystore ownership: customer-managed keys are the default for Private (VPC and on-prem). For VPC deployments we support bringing your own KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) and Redwood will never hold unencrypted customer key material. For on-prem, customers retain the keystore locally; Redwood's operator tooling only receives ciphertext and metadata.
- Operator access: Redwood operators do not have routine access to customer plaintext. Breakglass is permitted only for emergency remediation (security incident affecting service availability) and is gated by: dual approval (Security + Customer SRE), time-limited ephemeral credentials, full session recording, and audit log entry with ticket reference.
- Subprocessors: for Private deployments, because control plane pieces may run in our managed plane (unless you choose fully air-gapped install), a small set of subprocessors related to telemetry ingestion and support tooling may be engaged. Attached matrix enumerates those services and the data types touched.
- Recommended contract language: see attached DPA_Addendum template. We can insert a narrow operator-access clause and an explicit KMS custody schedule.

Attachments included: [Attachment: PrivDeploy_KeyMatrix.pdf (PDF, 48KB)], [Attachment: DPA_Addendum_Template.docx (DOCX, 42KB)], [Attachment: PrivDeploy_Runbook_Summary.txt (TXT, 6KB)]

Next steps I propose: 1) Review attachments with your legal/DPO, 2) We update the DPA addendum per feedback, 3) DocuSign and sign — I can expedite. If helpful we can run a 30-minute technical walkthrough with your SRE and DPO this week.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Forwarding Maya's thread. Quick internal notes to align on the responses Logan sent:

- KMS escrow: legal asked last quarter about explicit escrow language. Proposal: include an optional Appendix B that allows customer to request escrow only for on-prem cases where customer supplies hardware-backed keystores. We should avoid mandatory escrow language for VPC.
- Breakglass controls: implement a single Jira workflow (INFRA-1124) that records approvals (2 approvers), required ticket ID in audit log, and auto-expiration of credentials in 12 hours. Karthik, can infra put the enforced TTL in place for Private operator jobs?
- Subprocessors: confirm list in the attached KeyMatrix reflects the current infra — I counted three: observability vendor, helpdesk ticketing (support screenshots), and our monitoring agent (no PII). We should state 'telemetry limited to non-sensitive metadata' in the addendum.

Karthik — please confirm feasibility and I'll prepare language for Appendix B and the breakglass clause to hand to legal.

-Kimberly
Chief Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Hi Maria / Maya — thanks for the specific asks. Answers below and I've attached the redline-ready addendum plus a DocuSign link to sign if this matches your needs.

1) Subprocessor list: attached in PrivDeploy_KeyMatrix.pdf (sheet 2). Current subprocessors that may receive aggregated telemetry: Telemetrix Inc. (US), SupportFlow LLC (US), and MetricsEdge EU (Ireland). We include jurisdiction and data types touched in the matrix. If HelixMed prefers, we will commit to 30 days pre-notification for adding any new subprocessor that may touch telemetry for your Private deployment.

2) Cross-border flows: if customer-managed KMS is located in EU and Redwood's control plane (hosted) is in the US, we will not receive key material and therefore cannot decrypt content. Minimal operational metadata (request trace ids, request size, perf metrics) may be visible to the control plane for routing/availability. We propose a contractual data transfer clause that limits metadata export to operational metrics only and lists SCCs as applicable. If you prefer zero metadata export, we can propose a hybrid model where control plane is deployed in-region (Dedicated) or fully on-prem.

3) Operator obligations snippet (proposed):
"Redwood personnel will only perform emergency operator actions after: (a) documented approval from Customer SRE and Redwood Security (two approvers), (b) generation of ephemeral credentials that auto-revoke after a narrow TTL, and (c) full session recording and audit log entry referencing a ticket. All operator access events will be retained for 2 years and made available to the Customer upon request within 30 days. Redwood will notify Customer within 48 hours of any confirmed or suspected unauthorized operator access."

Attachments: [Attachment: PrivDeploy_KeyMatrix.pdf], [Attachment: DPA_Addendum_HelixMed_20261016.pdf]
DocuSign (if ready to sign): https://www.docusign.com/helloworld/sign?doc=HELIX-DPA-ADD-20261016

Next steps: 1) If the addendum language looks good, sign the DocuSign and we'll schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough to align on KMS configuration and the emergency access Jira workflow (INFRA-1124). 2) If you need redlines, send them and Kimberly & our legal will turn around within 48 hours.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the runbook.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
